rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punished person uses his face as a shield because his hands are chained to his neck, leaving no other way to ward off torment.
rows.anchor: يجعله درقة يقي به نفسه لأنه يكون يداه مغلولة إلى عنقه فلا يقدر أن يتقي إلا بوجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison is with someone safe from punishment; the predicate is omitted, as in similar constructions.
rows.anchor: كمن هو آمن منه، فحذف الخبر كما حذف في نظائره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The overt description wrongdoers replaces a pronoun to register their wrongdoing and identify why they are addressed this way.
rows.anchor: فوضع الظاهر موضعه تسجيلا عليهم بالظلم وإشعارا بالموجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are told to taste the consequence of what they earned; the waw is circumstantial with an implicit qad.
rows.anchor: أي وباله، والواو للحال وقد مقدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier peoples were struck by punishment from a direction they did not expect as a source of harm.
rows.anchor: من الجهة التي لا يخطر ببالهم أن الشر يأتيهم منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-khizy means humiliation, exemplified by transformation, being swallowed by the earth, killing, captivity, and exile.
rows.anchor: كالمسخ والخسف والقتل والسبي والإجلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepared punishment of the afterlife is greater in severity and duration; people capable of knowledge and reflection would recognize and learn from this.
rows.anchor: لو كانوا من أهل العلم والنظر لعلموا ذلك واعتبروا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What the benefactors wish for is theirs with their Lord in Paradise; this is their recompense for doing good.
rows.anchor: { لهم ما يشآءون عند ربهم } في الجنة

words: ليكفر الله عنهم أسوأ الذي عملوا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worst may intensify the promise: if the worst is expiated, lesser sins are more readily expiated too.
rows.anchor: خص الأسوأ للمبالغة فإنه إذا كفر كان غيره أولى بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the wording reflects believers' view of their sins: they regard themselves as deficient and even their minor faults as their worst sins.
rows.anchor: أو للإشعار بأنهم لاستعظامهم الذنوب يحسبون أنهم مقصرون مذنبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that aswaʾ means bad, as in the expression about the two most just of Marwan's sons.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بمعنى السيء كقولهم: الناقص والأشج أعدلا بني مروان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading takes aswaʾ as the plural of sūʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرىء«أسوأ» جمع سوء

words: ويجزيهم أجرهم بأحسن الذي كانوا يعملون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their good deeds are assessed at their best, increasing the reward in amount and excellence because of their great sincerity.
rows.anchor: فتعد لهم محاسن أعمالهم بأحسنها في زيادة الأجر وعظمه لفرط إخلاصهم فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative denies the negation, emphatically affirming that God suffices His servant.
rows.anchor: استفهام إنكار للنفي مبالغة في الإثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant may mean the Messenger of God, or the wording may be general; the latter is supported by the reading His servants, explained as the prophets.
rows.anchor: والعبد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ويحتمل الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threateners are Quraysh, who said they feared their idols would harm the Prophet because he criticized them.
rows.anchor: يعني قريشا فإنهم قالوا له إنا نخاف أن تخبلك آلهتنا بعيبك إياها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet sent Khalid to break al-Uzza; its custodian warned Khalid of the idol's force, so the threat to Khalid counted as a threat to the Prophet who sent him.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه بعث خالدا ليكسر العزى فقال له سادنها أحذركها

words: ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God misguides one who overlooks His sufficiency and fears what cannot benefit or harm; such a person has no guide to right conduct.
rows.anchor: حتى غفل عن كفاية الله له وخوفه بما لا ينفع ولا يضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This describes the human species according to its prevalent behavior; the fa connects the episode to their response when God alone is mentioned.
rows.anchor: إخبار عن الجنس بما يغلب فيه، والعطف على قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence exposes their reversal: they recoil from mentioning God alone and welcome mention of idols, yet in distress pray to the one they recoiled from.
rows.anchor: لبيان مناقضتهم وتعكيسهم في التسبب بمعنى أنهم يشمئزون عن ذكر الله وحده ويستبشرون بذكر الآلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intervening material is a parenthesis that reinforces the condemnation of this inconsistency.
rows.anchor: وما بينهما اعتراض مؤكد لإنكار ذلك عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khawwalah means that God grants the blessing as a favor; this act of granting is particular to God.
rows.anchor: أعطيناه إياه تفضلا فإن التخويل مختص به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that the speaker claims to know the means by which he earned the blessing.
rows.anchor: مني بوجوه كسبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he claims he knew he would receive it because he deserved it.
rows.anchor: أو بأني سأعطاه لما لي من استحقاقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation is that he attributes the gift to God's knowledge of his deserving it.
rows.anchor: أو من الله بي واستحقاقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to mā if that is relative; otherwise it refers to the blessing, with masculine agreement because the intended referent is a thing from it.
rows.anchor: والهاء فيه لما إن جعلت موصولة وإلا فللنعمة والتذكير لأن المراد شيء منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing is a test of whether its recipient will be grateful or ungrateful, refuting his claim that it proves his merit.
rows.anchor: امتحان له أيشكر أم يكفر، وهو رد لما قاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun agrees either with the predicate or with the word niʿma; a masculine reading is also reported.
rows.anchor: الخير أو لفظ ال { نعمة } ، وقرىء بالتذكير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people do not know that the blessing is a test; this confirms that the human is used generically.
rows.anchor: ذلك، وهو دليل على أن الإنسان للجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun refers to the claim I was given it on account of knowledge, understood as a word or sentence; a masculine reading is also reported.
rows.anchor: الهاء لقوله { إنما أوتيته على علم } لأنها كلمة أو جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier claimants are Qarun and his people, who voiced and approved his claim.
rows.anchor: قارون وقومه فإنه قال ورضي به قومه

words: فما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يكسبون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their worldly possessions and gains did not benefit them.
rows.anchor: من متاع الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each soul is given the recompense for its deeds; God knows what they do, so no act escapes Him.
rows.anchor: جزاءه. { وهو أعلم بما يفعلون } فلا يفوته شيء

words: وسيق الذين كفروا إلى جهنم زمرا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers are driven in successive, separate groups, differing in the degrees of their misguidance and wickedness.
rows.anchor: أفواجا متفرقة بعضها في أثر بعض على تفاوت أقدامهم في الضلالة والشرارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zumrah may derive from zamr, sound, since a group makes noise; alternatively it denotes a small group, by comparison with words for sparse wool or scant manliness.
rows.anchor: واشتقاقها من الزمر وهو الصوت إذ الجماعة لا تخلو عنه، أو من قولهم شاة زمرة قليلة الشعر ورجل زمر قليل المروءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gates are opened for the groups to enter; hatta introduces and depicts the sentence that follows.
rows.anchor: و { حتى } وهي التي تحكي بعدها الجملة

rows.speaker: الكوفون
rows.claim: The Kufans read فتحت with a light ta.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكوفين «فتحت» بتخفيف التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardians address them to rebuke and reproach them.
rows.anchor: تقريعا وتوبيخا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers were from your own kind.
rows.anchor: من جنسكم

words: يتلون عليكم آيات ربكم وينذرونكم لقاء يومكم هذا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers recited God's signs and warned of the encounter on this day, meaning the time when the condemned enter Hell.
rows.anchor: وقتكم هذا وهو وقت دخولهم النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reproach links culpability to the arrival of messengers and delivery of scripture, evidence that there is no obligation before revealed law.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أنه لا تكليف قبل الشرع من حيث إنهم عللوا توبيخهم بإتيان الرسل وتبليغ الكتب

words: قالوا بلى ولكن حقت كلمة العذاب على الكافرين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They concede the messengers came, but God's judgment of wretchedness and Hell has become binding on them; the disbelievers replaces a pronoun to specify who is condemned.
rows.anchor: كلمة الله بالعذاب علينا وهو الحكم عليهم بالشقاوة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative identifies the word of punishment with God's declaration that He will fill Hell with jinn and people.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو قوله لأملان جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker is left unnamed to make the command sound more formidable.
rows.anchor: أبهم القائل لتهويل ما يقال لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned abode is a bad resting place; the generic definite article in the arrogant points back to those already mentioned.
rows.anchor: اللام فيه للجنس والمخصوص بالذم سبق ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling arrogance the reason for their abode does not conflict with their entry being decreed: arrogance and their other vices result from that decree, as the Prophet's report about destiny and deeds explains.
rows.anchor: ولا ينافي إشعاره بأن مثواهم في النار لتكبرهم عن الحق أن يكون دخولهم فيها لأن كلمة العذاب حقت عليهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says that a person destined for Paradise is enabled to do its people's deeds until death, while one destined for the Fire is enabled to do its people's deeds until death.
rows.anchor: إن الله تعالى إذا خلق العبد للجنة استعمله بعمل أهل الجنة، حتى يموت على عمل من أعمال أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's followers tried to restrain him, saying Moses was only a magician and not the danger Pharaoh feared.
rows.anchor: كانوا يكفونه عن قتله ويقولون إنه ليس الذي تخافه بل هو ساحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's attempt to justify killing Moses despite his readiness to kill over trivial matters suggests he knew Moses was a prophet; alternatively, he thought the attempt would not be possible.
rows.anchor: وتعلله بذلك مع كونه سفاكا في أهون شيء دليل على أنه تيقن أنه نبي فخاف من قتله، أو ظن أنه لو حاوله لم يتيسر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Let him call his Lord conveys Pharaoh's bravado and professed indifference to Moses' prayer.
rows.anchor: فإنه تجلد وعدم مبالاة بدعائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh says he fears Moses will change their religion from worship of Pharaoh and idols, as the verse cited from al-Aʿrāf indicates.
rows.anchor: أن يغير ما أنتم عليه من عبادته وعبادة الأصنام

words: أو أن يظهر في الأرض الفساد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged corruption is worldly conflict and disorder if Moses cannot abolish their religion altogether.
rows.anchor: ما يفسد دنياكم من التحارب والتهارج إن لم يقدر أن يبطل دينكم بالكلية

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
rows.claim: These readers use waw, presenting the two fears as a combined possibility.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر بالواو على معنى الجمع

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر والكوفيون غير حفص
rows.claim: These readers open the ya and ha and put al-fasad in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وابن كثير وابن عامر والكوفيون غير حفص بفتح الياء والهاء ورفع الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses addresses his people after hearing Pharaoh's words.
rows.anchor: أي لقومه لما سمع بكلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic opening signals that seeking refuge in God is the decisive means of warding off harm.
rows.anchor: صدر الكلام بأن تأكيدا وإشعارا على أن السبب المؤكد في دفع الشر هو العياذ بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses uses Lord because he asks for protection and care, and says my Lord and yours to urge agreement, since shared spiritual orientation helps bring a response.
rows.anchor: وخص اسم الرب لأن المطلوب هو الحفظ والتربية، وإضافته إليه وإليهم حثا لهم على موافقته لما في تظاهر الأرواح من استجلاب الإجابة

words: من كل متكبر لا يؤمن بيوم الحساب
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses does not name Pharaoh, but describes a general class to broaden the refuge and observe propriety while identifying what motivates him.
rows.anchor: ولم يسم فرعون وذكر وصفا يعمه وغيره لتعميم الاستعاذة ورعاية الحق والدلالة على الحامل له على القول

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي ونافع
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi assimilate the consonants in ʿudhtu here and in al-Dukhān; the same is also reported from Nafi.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي { عذت } فيه

words: وقال رجل مؤمن من آل فرعون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From Pharaoh's family may mean his relatives; alternatively, it attaches to concealing his faith, and the man was an Israelite or a foreign monotheist feigning agreement.
rows.anchor: من أقاربه. وقيل { من } متعلق بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means, Are you deliberately seeking to kill a man?
rows.anchor: أتقصدون قتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean because he says or at the time he says, without reflection or consideration.
rows.anchor: لأن يقول، أو وقت أن يقول من غير روية وتأمل في أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: My Lord is God means God alone, with the same restrictive force as my friend is Zayd.
rows.anchor: وحده وهو في الدلالة على الحصر مثل صديقي زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The numerous proofs are miracles and demonstrations that establish Moses' truthfulness.
rows.anchor: المتكثرة الدالة على صدقه من المعجزات والاستدلالات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the signs from your Lord presses them to acknowledge the point and gently leads them toward admitting it.
rows.anchor: أضافه إليهم بعد ذكر البينات احتجاجا عليهم واستدراجا لهم إلى الاعتراف به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Moses lies, the harm of his lie falls only on him, so there is no need to kill him to avert it.
rows.anchor: لا يتخطاه وبال كذبه فيحتاج في دفعه إلى قتله

words: وإن يك صادقا يصبكم بعض الذي يعدكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At least part of the threatened punishment will befall them; warning them with a limited share is rhetorically forceful and displays fairness rather than bias.
rows.anchor: فلا أقل من أن يصيبكم بعضه، وفيه مبالغة في التحذير وإظهار للإنصاف وعدم التعصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some means some of the worldly punishment Moses promised, a portion of his threats and the more plausible outcome for the audience.
rows.anchor: أو يصبكم ما يعدكم من عذاب الدنيا وهو بعض مواعيده، كأنه خوفهم بما هو أظهر احتمالا عندهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interpreting some as all by appeal to Labīd's verse is rejected: Labīd meant himself by some of the souls.
rows.anchor: وتفسير ال { بعض } بالكل كقول لبيد:

words: إن الله لا يهدي من هو مسرف كذاب
rows.speaker: الرجل المؤمن
rows.claim: The believer's third argument has two sides: God would not guide and support a liar with signs, and someone God abandons will be destroyed without needing the audience to kill him.
rows.anchor: احتجاج ثالث ذو وجهين: أحدهما: أنه لو كان مسرفا كذابا

words: لكم الملك اليوم ظاهرين في الأرض
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker describes them as currently dominant and elevated in the land of Egypt.
rows.anchor: غالبين عالين. { في الأرض } أرض مصر

words: فمن ينصرنا من بأس الله إن جاءنا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should not endanger themselves by killing Moses, since no one could protect them from God's might if it came.
rows.anchor: أي فلا تفسدوا أمركم ولا تتعرضوا لبأس الله بقتله فإنه إن جاءنا لم يمنعنا منه أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer includes himself in us because he is related to them and wants to show solidarity with those he advises.
rows.anchor: وإنما أدرج نفسه في الضميرين لأنه كان منهم في القرابة وليريهم أنه معهم ومساهمهم فيما ينصح لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh says he advises only what he himself approves, and tells them only what he considers correct, claiming his heart and tongue agree.
rows.anchor: ما أشير عليكم. { إلا ما أرى } وأستصوبه من قتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-rashād means the path of correctness; a doubled reading is intensive, derived from rashada or rushda, not from arshada.
rows.anchor: طريق الصواب، وقرىء بالتشديد على أنه فعال للمبالغة من رشد كعلام، أو من رشد كعباد لا من أرشد كجبار

words: إن الله لا يهدي من هو مسرف كذاب
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer likely intended the first argument while suggesting the second to soften their resistance; he also hints that Pharaoh is the extravagant liar whom God will not guide.
rows.anchor: ولعله أراد به المعنى الأول وخيل إليهم الثاني لتلين شكيمتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase asks the listener to recall the time when the people of Hell dispute; grammatically it may connect to the earlier they come in the morning.
rows.anchor: واذكر وقت تخاصمهم فيها ويحتمل العطف على غدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weak say they had been dependent followers of the arrogant.
rows.anchor: تفصيل له. { إنا كنا لكم تبعا } تباعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabaʿan may be a plural like khadam for khādim, or an elided or figurative expression for people who follow.
rows.anchor: تباعا كخدم في جمع خادم أو ذوي تبع بمعنى أتباع على الإضمار أو التجوز

words: فهل أنتم مغنون عنا نصيبا من النار
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask whether the arrogant can remove a share of the Fire from them or carry it in their place.
rows.anchor: بالدفع أو الحمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naṣīban may be an object supplied by the sense of avail, or a cognate-like object; on the latter analysis, min is governed by avail, like the construction in 3:116.
rows.anchor: مفعول به لما دل عليه { مغنون } أوله بالتضمين أو مصدر كشيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arrogant answer that both groups are in the Fire; even if they could, they would first have saved themselves.
rows.anchor: نحن وأنتم فكيف نغني عنكم ولو قدرنا لأغنينا عن أنفسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has kallan, as emphasis meaning all of us, with its nunation replacing the omitted possessive complement.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «كلا» على التأكيد لأنه بمعنى كلنا وتنوينه عوض عن المضاف إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallan cannot be parsed as a circumstantial accusative of the pronoun in the prepositional phrase, since that phrase cannot govern an anticipatory circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز جعله حالا من المستكن في الظرف فإنه لا يعمل في الحال المتقدمة

words: إن الله قد حكم بين العباد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has judged between servants by admitting the people of Paradise to Paradise and the people of Hell to Hell; His decree cannot be overturned.
rows.anchor: بأن أدخل أهل الجنة الجنة وأهل النار النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit name Jahannam replaces a pronoun either to intensify dread or to identify their location in it, perhaps its deepest level.
rows.anchor: ووضع { جهنم } موضع الضمير للتهويل

words: ادعوا ربكم يخفف عنا يوما من العذاب
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested day may mean an amount of time, with some of the punishment specifying it; alternatively, day is the object with an omitted genitive.
rows.anchor: قدر يوم. { من العذاب } شيئا من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardians invoke the messengers' clear proofs to make the inmates acknowledge the evidence and rebuke them for wasting their opportunity to pray and neglecting means of response.
rows.anchor: أرادوا به إلزامهم للحجة وتوبيخهم على إضاعتهم أوقات الدعاء وتعطيلهم أسباب الإجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardians say they themselves dare not pray because they have not been permitted to intercede for people like the inmates, thereby making them despair of an answer.
rows.anchor: فإنا لا نجترىء فيه إذ لم يؤذن لنا في الدعاء لأمثالكم، وفيه إقناط لهم عن الإجابة

words: وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' prayer is fruitless and will not be answered; the statement further extinguishes their hope of an answer.
rows.anchor: ضياع لا يجاب، وفيه اقناط لهم عن الإجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God aids messengers and believers through proof, victory, and requital of their opponents, both in this life and on the Day of Witnesses.
rows.anchor: بالحجة والظفر والانتقام لهم من الكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Witnesses are those who testify about people on the Resurrection Day: angels, prophets, and believers.
rows.anchor: و { الأشهد } جمع شاهد كصاحب وأصحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their enemies' occasional victories do not disprove the promise: outcomes and the prevailing course are what count.
rows.anchor: ولا ينتقض ذلك بما كان لأعدائهم عليهم من الغلبة أحيانا إذ العبرة بالعواقب وغالب الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istawā ilā means to direct oneself toward a place with undivided attention, as in ordinary Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: قصد نحوها من قولهم استوى إلى مكان كذا إذا توجه إليه توجها لا يلوي على غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma marks the difference in rank between the two creations, not a time delay, since Earth was spread after that before its mountains were formed.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن ثم لتفاوت ما بين الخلقتين لا للتراخي في المدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky's smoke is a dark substance, perhaps its material or the minute particles from which it was composed.
rows.anchor: أمر ظلماني، ولعله أراد به مادتها أو الأجزاء المتصغرة التي كتب منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that heaven and Earth are told to manifest the effects and varied beings placed within them.
rows.anchor: بما خلقت فيكما من التأثير والتأثر وأبرزا ما أودعتكما من الأوضاع المختلفة والكائنات المتنوعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they are ordered to come into existence, with the earlier creation understood as determination or ordering by rank.
rows.anchor: في الوجود على أن الخلق السابق بمعنى التقدير أو الترتيب للرتبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that the sky's coming is its coming-to-be while Earth's coming is its becoming spread, though the author notes the difficulty of this view.
rows.anchor: أو الإخبار أو إتيان السماء حدوثها وإتيان الأرض أن تصير مدحوة، وقد عرفت ما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further account has each come to cooperate with the other in producing what God intends.
rows.anchor: أو لتأت كل منكما الأخرى في حدوث ما أريد توليده منكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading ataya, from mutual cooperation, supports the interpretation that heaven and Earth should agree in carrying out God's intention.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده قراءة «آتيا» في المؤاتاة أي لتوافق كل واحدة أختها فيما أردت منكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether they will or refuse, the wording displays God's complete power and the inevitability of His will; it does not attribute actual willingness or aversion to them.
rows.anchor: شئتما ذلك أو أبيتما والمراد إظهار كمال قدرته ووجوب وقوع مراده لا إثبات الطوع والكره لهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal nouns ṭawʿan and karhan function as circumstantial expressions.
rows.anchor: وهما مصدران وقعا موقع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply most likely pictures God's power affecting the two and their inherent response, portraying them as a master obeyed by a servant, like Be, and it is.
rows.anchor: والأظهر أن المراد تصوير تأثير قدرته فيهما وتأثرهما بالذات عنها، وتمثيلهما بأمر المطاع وإجابة المطيع الطائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine plural ṭāʾiʿīn follows semantic treatment of the two as addressed beings, as in the cited form sājidīn.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال طائعين على المعنى باعتبار كونهما مخاطبتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nazgh is a prod or prick; Satan's whispering is likened to it because it stirs a person toward improper conduct, such as responding to harm with something worse.
rows.anchor: نخس شبه به وسوسته لأنها تبعث الإنسان على ما لا ينبغي كالدفع بما هو أسوأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nazgh may be cast in a novel active form, or function as a verbal noun describing Satan as the one who prods.
rows.anchor: وجعل النزغ نازغا على طريقة جديدة، أو أريد به نازغ وصفا للشيطان بالمصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seek God's protection from Satan's evil and do not obey him.
rows.anchor: من شره ولا تطعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears the plea for refuge and knows either the person's intention or what is right for him.
rows.anchor: { العليم } بنيتك أو بصلاحك

words: ومن ءايته اليل والنهار والشمس والقمر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night, day, sun, and moon are signs of God.
rows.anchor: ومن ءايته اليل والنهار والشمس والقمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are creatures subject to command, just as humans are, so they are not to be worshipped.
rows.anchor: لأنهما مخلوقان مأموران مثلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to all four preceding signs; mentioning them together suggests that they belong among things without knowledge or choice.
rows.anchor: الضمير للأربعة المذكورة، والمقصود تعليق الفعل بهما إشعارا بأنهما من عداد ما لا يعلم ولا يختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship God who created them; prostration is the most specific form of worship.
rows.anchor: فإن السجود أخص العبادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author places the prostration of recitation at this verse because it contains the command; Abu Hanifa places it at the end of the following verse, where the meaning is complete.
rows.anchor: وهو موضع السجود عندنا لاقتران الأمر به، وعند أبي حنيفة آخر الآية الأخرى لأنه تمام المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God responds to them is understood with an omitted lam, as in the cited construction in al-Mutaffifin.
rows.anchor: أي يستجيب الله لهم فحذف اللام كما حذف في وإذا كالوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yastajibu may mean that God answers their prayers or rewards their obedience, which functions like a request for its outcome.
rows.anchor: والمراد إجابة الدعاء أو الإثابة على الطاعة، فإنها كدعاء وطلب لما يترتب عليها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report calls praise of God the best supplication.
rows.anchor:
ومنه قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام
" أفضل الدعاء الحمد لله "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, believers respond to God by obeying Him when He calls them to obedience.
rows.anchor: أو يستجيبون لله بالطاعة إذا دعاهم إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grants them more of His favor than what they asked for, earned, or made themselves deserving of through their response.
rows.anchor: على ما سألوا واستحقوا واستوجبوا له بالاستجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers receive severe punishment in place of the believers' reward and additional favor.
rows.anchor: بدل ما للمؤمنين من الثواب والتفضل

words: ولو بسط الله الرزق لعباده لبغوا في الأرض
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If provision were expanded, people would grow arrogant and corrupt through excess; alternatively, some would dominate and oppress others. This describes the prevalent pattern.
rows.anchor: لتكبروا وأفسدوا فيها بطرا، أو لبغى بعضهم على بعض استيلاء واستعلاء وهذا على الغالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root baghy means seeking to go beyond moderation in the quantity or quality of what one pursues.
rows.anchor: وأصل البغي طلب تجاوز الاقتصاد فيما يتحرى كمية أو كيفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God measures provision according to His will and knowledge of people's hidden and evident states, allotting what suits their circumstances.
rows.anchor: يعلم خفايا أمرهم وجلايا حالهم فيقدر لهم ما يناسب شأنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says the verse came down after the People of the Bench wished for wealth.
rows.anchor: روي أن أهل الصفة تمنوا الغنى فنزلت

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says Arabs would fight when conditions were fertile and migrate in search of pasture during drought.
rows.anchor: وقيل في العرب كانوا إذا أخصبوا تحاربوا وإذا أجدبوا انتجعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghayth is rain that rescues people from drought, so the word is reserved for beneficial rain.
rows.anchor: المطر الذي يغيثهم من الجدب ولذلك خص بالنافع

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وعاصم
rows.claim: Nafiʿ, Ibn ʿAmir, and ʿAsim read the verb with a doubled zāy.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر وعاصم «ينزل» بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaniṭū means that they despaired of rain; a reading pronounces the nūn with kasra.
rows.anchor: أيسوا منه، وقرىء بكسر النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God spreads His mercy through plains, mountains, plants, and animals.
rows.anchor: في كل شيء من السهل والجبل والنبات والحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is the guardian who cares for His servants graciously and spreads mercy, and is therefore deserving of praise.
rows.anchor: { الحميد } المستحق للحمد على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens and Earth, in their essences and properties, point to an existing creator who is powerful and wise.
rows.anchor: فإنها بذاتها وصفاتها تدل على وجود صانع قادر حكيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What He dispersed in them may coordinate with the heavens or with the creation.
rows.anchor: عطف على { السموات } أو ال { خلق }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dābbah may mean any living being, naming the cause by its effect; alternatively, it means creatures that move on Earth, with what is in either of the two counted as being in them.
rows.anchor: من حي على إطلاق اسم المسبب على السبب، أو مما يدب على الأرض وما يكون في أحد الشيئين يصدق أن فيها في الجملة

words: وهو على جمعهم إذا يشاء قدير
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can gather them at any time He wills.
rows.anchor: أي في أي وقت يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idhā can introduce the past as well as the present tense.
rows.anchor: كما تدخل على الماضي تدخل على المضارع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh either invited his people to comply readily or made their minds and judgment lightweight.
rows.anchor: فطلب منهم الخفة في مطاوعته أو فاستخف أحلامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They obeyed Pharaoh in what he ordered because they were a wicked people.
rows.anchor: فيما أمرهم به { إنهم كانوا قوما فسقين } فلذلك أطاعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They angered God through extreme obstinacy and disobedience; the verb derives from becoming intensely angry.
rows.anchor: أغضبونا بالإفراط في العناد والعصيان منقول من أسف إذا اشتد غضبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God retaliated against them by drowning them all in the sea.
rows.anchor: اشتد غضبه. { انتقمنا منهم فأغرقنهم أجمعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They became a precedent for later disbelievers, who could follow their example in deserving a similar punishment; salaf may be a verbal noun used adjectivally or a plural of sālif.
rows.anchor: قدوة لمن بعدهم من الكفار يقتدون به في استحقاق مثل عقابهم، مصدر نعت به أو جمع سالف

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read with ḍamma on both consonants, explained as a plural of salīf, sālif, or salaf; other forms vary the vowel or derive it from sulfah, a group already gone.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي بضم السين واللام جمع سليف كرغف ورغيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They became a lesson or a remarkable story for later people, summed up by saying, “Your likeness is that of Pharaoh's people.”
rows.anchor: وعظة لهم أو قصة عجيبة تسير مسير الأمثال لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those excepted are people God shows mercy by forgiving and accepting intercession for them.
rows.anchor: بالعفو عنه وقبول الشفاعة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may be nominative as a substitute for the wāw or accusative as an exception.
rows.anchor: ومحله الرفع على البدل من الواو والنصب على الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's might prevents anyone from protecting those He intends to punish; His mercy belongs to those He intends to show mercy.
rows.anchor: لا ينصر منه من أراد تعذيبه. { الرحيم } لمن أراد أن يرحمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading pronounces the shīn in shajarat al-zaqqūm with kasra; its explanation was given earlier in al-Ṣāffāt.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بكسر الشين ومعنى { الزقوم } سبق في «الصافات»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The athīm is the person burdened with many sins; the intended referent is a disbeliever, as the surrounding verses show.
rows.anchor: الكثير الآثام، والمراد به الكافر لدلالة ما قبله وما بعده عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhl may be a substance heated until it melts in the Fire, or the dregs of oil.
rows.anchor: وهو ما يمهل في النار حتى يذوب. وقيل دردي الزيت

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وحفص ورويس
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Hafs, and Ruways read yaghli with yāʾ; its pronoun refers to the food or Zaqqum, not the melted substance, since the clause is circumstantial.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وحفص ورويس بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It boils with a boiling like that of intensely hot water.
rows.anchor: غليانا مثل غليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command presupposes an unspoken “they said,” and its addressees are the wardens of Hell.
rows.anchor: على إرادة القول والمقول له الزبانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAtl means to seize something by its parts and drag it forcibly; here the command is to drag him.
rows.anchor: فجروه والعتل الأخذ بمجامع الشيء وجره بقهر

rows.speaker: الحجازيان وابن عامر ويعقوب
rows.claim: The Hijazis, Ibn ʿAmir, and Yaʿqub read the verb with ḍamma; the two forms are dialectal variants.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحجازيان وابن عامر ويعقوب بالضم وهما لغتان. { إلى سواء الجحيم } وسطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawāʾ al-jaḥīm means the middle of the blazing Fire.
rows.anchor: وهما لغتان. { إلى سواء الجحيم } وسطه

words: ثم صبوا فوق رأسه من عذاب الحميم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An original image of boiling water poured from above their heads is recast as punishment that is boiling water for emphasis; the genitive construction lightens the wording, and min indicates a portion of that kind.
rows.anchor: كان أصله يصب من فوق رؤوسهم الحميم فقيل يصب من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardians say this mockingly to taunt him with the claim to honor and might he used to make.
rows.anchor: أي وقولوا له ذلك استهزاء به وتفريعا على ما كان يزعمه

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads anna with fatḥ, construing it as taste because you are or connecting it with an omitted punishment.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي «أنك» بالفتح أي ذق لأنك أو { عذاب }

words: إن هذا ما كنتم به تمترون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment is what they used to doubt and dispute.
rows.anchor: ما كنتم به تمترون } تشكون وتمارون فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqām means a place of residence; Nafiʿ and Ibn ʿAmir read it with ḍamma on the mīm.
rows.anchor: في موضع إقامة، وقرأ نافع وابن عامر بضم الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The residence is secure for its inhabitant from harm and displacement.
rows.anchor: يأمن صاحبه عن الآفة والانتقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gardens and springs are apposition to the place of residence, clarifying its purity and its provision of pleasurable food and drink.
rows.anchor: بدل من مقام جيء به للدلالة على نزاهته، واشتماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The listeners are hypocrites who attended the Messenger's gathering and heard him speak.
rows.anchor: يعني المنافقين كانوا يحضرون مجلس الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم ويسمعون كلامه

words: قالوا للذين أوتوا العلم ماذا قال آنفا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those given knowledge are the learned Companions.
rows.anchor: أي لعلماء الصحابة رضي الله تعالى عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their question may be mocking; alternatively, they ask what the Messenger just said because they did not listen attentively out of disregard.
rows.anchor: ما الذي قال الساعة، استهزاء أو استعلاما إذا لم يلقوا له آذانهم تهاونا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ānifan means just now, derived from the front of a thing and borrowed from the nose; the related verbs mean to begin anew.
rows.anchor: من قولهم أنف الشيء لما تقدم منه مستعار من الجارحة، ومنه استأنف وائتنف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ānifan functions either as an adverb meaning a newly begun time or as a circumstantial expression attached to the pronoun in he said.
rows.anchor: وهو ظرف بمعنى وقتا مؤتنفا، أو حال من الضمير في { قال }

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the word as anfa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير «أنفا»

words: أولئك الذين طبع الله على قلوبهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sealed their hearts and they followed their desires, which is why they mocked and disregarded the Messenger's speech.
rows.anchor: فلذلك استهزؤوا وتهاونوا بكلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God increases the guidance of those already guided through enabling grace and inspiration, or through the Messenger's words.
rows.anchor: أي زادهم الله بالتوفيق والإلهام، أو قول الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives them their taqwā by explaining what to avoid, helping them practice it, or granting its reward.
rows.anchor: بين لهم ما يتقون أو أعانهم على تقواهم، أو أعطاهم جزاءها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People descend either from Adam and Eve or, distributively, from a father and mother; all are equal in this respect, so lineage is no basis for boasting.
rows.anchor: من آدم وحواء عليهما السلام، أو خلقنا كل واحد منكم من أب وأم فالكل سواء في ذلك فلا وجه للتفاخر بالنسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shared origin may also affirm brotherhood that restrains people from backbiting.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون تقريرا للأخوة المانعة عن الاغتياب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A shaʿb is a large group tracing to one origin and contains tribes; tribes contain clans, clans subclans, subclans branches, and branches families. The cited examples progress from Khuzaima and Kinana to Quraysh, Qusay, Hashim, and Abbas.
rows.anchor: الشعب الجمع العظيم المنتسبون إلى أصل واحد وهو يجمع القبائل. والقبيلة تجمع العمائر. والعمارة تجمع البطون. والبطن تجمع الأفخاذ. والفخذ يجمع الفضائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the shaʿbs are subdivisions of non-Arabs, while Arab peoples are organized as tribes.
rows.anchor: وقبل الشعوب بطون العجم والقبائل بطون العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose is mutual recognition, not pride in forefathers or tribal identity.
rows.anchor: ليعرف بعضكم بعضا لا للتفاخر بالآباء والقبائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is read with assimilation as lataʿrafū, and also as litatārafū or lataʿrafū.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { لتعرفوا } بالإدغام و «لتتعارفوا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most honored before God is the most godfearing, since taqwā perfects souls and differentiates people; whoever seeks honor should seek it through taqwā.
rows.anchor: فإن التقوى بها تكمل النفوس وتتفاضل بها الأشخاص، فمن أراد شرفا فليلتمسه منها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says that whoever wants to be the most honored of people should fear God.
rows.anchor: كما قال عليه الصلاة والسلام " من سره أن يكون أكرم الناس فليتق الله "

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report divides people into a pious believer, honored by God, and a wicked wretch, debased before God.
rows.anchor:
وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام
" يا أيها الناس إنما الناس رجلان مؤمن تقي كريم على الله، وفاجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows people and is aware of their inner realities.
rows.anchor: { إن الله عليم } بكم { خبير } ببواطنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The occasion was a group of Banu Asad arriving in Medina during a drought, professing the two testimonies, and reminding the Messenger that they had brought dependents and had not fought as another tribe had, while seeking alms.
rows.anchor: نزلت في نفر من بني أسد قدموا المدينة في سنة جدبة وأظهروا الشهادتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They had not believed in the inward sense of assent with confidence and a tranquil heart; their claim that they had benefited the Messenger betrayed their attitude.
rows.anchor: إذ الإيمان تصديق مع ثقة وطمأنينة قلب، ولم يحصل لكم إلا لما مننتم على الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام بالإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam means submission and entry into peace, outward profession of the two testimonies, and desisting from fighting.
rows.anchor: فإن الإسلام انقياد ودخول في السلم وإظهار الشهادتين وترك المحاربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording avoids directly forbidding their claim to faith or making an unqualified ruling that they had submitted, since the legal condition for recognizing that claim was absent.
rows.anchor: فعدل منه إلى هذا النظم احترازا من النهي عن القول بالإيمان والجزم بإسلامهم، وقد فقد شرط اعتباره شرعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This clause specifies the timing of say: their hearts had not yet come into agreement with their tongues.
rows.anchor: توقيت ل { قولوا } فإنه حال من ضميره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obedience means sincerity and abandoning hypocrisy; it will not diminish any of their deeds' reward.
rows.anchor: بالإخلاص وترك النفاق. { لا يلتكم من أعملكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yalitkum means will not diminish you; the verb latta means to reduce.
rows.anchor: من لات يليت ليتا إذا نقص

rows.speaker: البصريان
rows.claim: The two Basran readers use yaʾaltkum, from al-alt, a dialect of Ghatafan.
rows.anchor: وقرأ البصريان «لا يألتكم» من الألت وهو لغة غطفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forgives obedient people for their past failings and shows mercy by favoring them.
rows.anchor: لما فرط من المطيعين. { رحيم } بالتفضل عليهم
